//: Copy-paste detection (jscpd, token-based Rabin-Karp). Run it with:
npx jscpd@5.0.12 --config .jscpd.json      (or `npm run dup` from web/)
CI runs the same command, so the `threshold` below is a real gate: duplication cannot
grow past it. Lower it when a refactor brings the number down; raising it needs a reason
in the commit, the same rule the coverage floor follows.
min-lines 10 / min-tokens 60 is deliberately not sensitive: below that it reports every
`match` arm and every three-line builder, which is noise rather than duplication. What it
does catch at this setting has been worth catching — five copies of a Braille spinner
table, two identical dtype/shape span builders, the same unsafe HDF5 buffer handoff in two
filters, and a 40-line render tail (rect clamping included) in two screen renderers.
Tests are excluded: a test's whole job is to spell the case out, and near-identical
fixtures are usually clearer than a parameterised helper.
`threshold` is compared against the duplicated-**TOKEN** percentage, not the line one.
The console table prints both and the failure message rounds to one decimal, which makes
it easy to reason about the wrong column: at 0.75 lines / 0.81 tokens it fails, reporting
'0.8% over threshold (0.8%)'. Read the tokens figure when deciding this number.
The threshold sits just above the measurement, not at a round number: 1.0 would have
allowed a large amount of new duplication before firing, which is not a ratchet. History:
0.8 (tokens 0.74) → 0.75 (tokens 0.74, after the engine took over the screens' overlay
slot) → 0.80 (tokens 0.79, when the compare screen was added).
That last one is a RAISE, so it owes a reason. A new screen necessarily adds one more
instance of the `Mode` trait's required shape — on_enter / pre_draw / render_frame /
open_palette / set_scroll / residual — and those are method signatures the trait mandates.
Collapsing them needs the trait redesign that `explorer/mod.rs` documents as deliberately
deferred. What was NOT left duplicated: the compare screen's arrival first pushed this to
0.89, and four genuinely shared behaviours came out of that (`scroll_key`, `scroll_wheel`,
`report_key` for the legend/quit/back/forward arms, and `common_hint_tail` for the footer
every screen ends with) before the number was moved.
